name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
shortDescription: Singapore’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site with 165+ years of botanical heritage.
description: Founded in 1859, the Singapore Botanic Gardens is a 82-hectare tropical garden and the only tropical botanical garden on the UNESCO World Heritage list. It encompasses the historic National Orchid Garden, an ancient 6-hectare primary rainforest remnant older than the city itself, and the Keppel Discovery Wetlands in the Learning Forest.
accessibilityInfo: Smooth paved pathways throughout the main grounds. Wheelchair rentals are available at Tanglin, Nassim, and Bukit Timah visitor services. Tactile ground surface indicators on key heritage trails.

name: Gardens by the Bay
shortDescription: Futuristic botanical architecture housing over 1.5 million plants from global biomes.
description: A 101-hectare horticultural marvel featuring the iconic Supertree Grove, the Flower Dome (the world’s largest glass greenhouse), and the misty Cloud Forest with a 35-metre tall mountain covered in lush epiphytes, bromeliads, and highland pitcher plants. Designed with integrated environmental engineering, including biomass energy co-generation and rainwater harvesting lakes.
accessibilityInfo: Barrier-free access across all outdoor gardens and conservatories. Elevators provide access to the Cloud Forest walkways and OCBC Skyway. Mobility scooter and stroller loans available.

name: MacRitchie Reservoir & Central Catchment
shortDescription: Singapore’s oldest reservoir bordered by pristine primary and mature secondary rainforest.
description: The crown jewel of Singapore’s green heart. The Central Catchment Nature Reserve covers over 2,000 hectares of forest surrounding MacRitchie Reservoir. Miles of hiking trails wind through dipterocarp forests, leading to the 250-metre free-standing TreeTop Walk suspension bridge, offering panoramic canopy views 25 metres above the forest floor.
accessibilityInfo: Boardwalks near the reservoir entrance (Chemperai and Prunus trails) are gently graded and barrier-free. Deep forest hiking trails (TreeTop Walk loop) feature rugged uneven terrain, tree roots, and steep stairs.
openingHours: 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM daily (TreeTop Walk closed on Mondays except public holidays)

name: Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve
shortDescription: ASEAN Heritage Park with sprawling mangrove ecosystems and migratory shorebird roosts.
description: Singapore’s first ASEAN Heritage Park spanning 202 hectares of mangroves, mudflats, and secondary forest. Situated along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, it provides critical stopover feeding grounds for thousands of migratory shorebirds between September and March, alongside resident estuarine crocodiles and mudskippers.
accessibilityInfo: The Wetland Centre and Visitor Centre trails (Junior Adventure Trail and Mangrove Boardwalk) are barrier-free with ramps. The deeper Migratory Bird Trail has gravel paths and raised wooden bird-watching screens.

name: Bukit Timah Nature Reserve
shortDescription: Singapore’s highest natural hill cloaked in ancient primary tropical rainforest.
description: Rising 163 metres above sea level, Bukit Timah contains more tree species in its 163 hectares than the entire continent of North America. An ASEAN Heritage Park, it preserves Singapore’s primary dipterocarp rainforest with towering Seraya trees, freshwater streams, and rare endemic invertebrates.
accessibilityInfo: Main Visitor Centre is wheelchair accessible. Summit Main Path is a paved steep incline (approx 15% gradient). Forest side-trails are natural dirt paths with granite rock steps.

name: The Southern Ridges & Henderson Waves
shortDescription: A 10-km elevated panoramic canopy trail connecting five southern coastal ridge parks.
description: An inspiring 10-kilometre continuous green corridor linking Mount Faber Park, Telok Blangah Hill Park, HortPark, Kent Ridge Park, and Labrador Nature Reserve. Features include the Forest Walk—an elevated steel mesh walkway through canopy layers—and Henderson Waves, the highest pedestrian bridge in Singapore with sculpted timber rib structures.
accessibilityInfo: Henderson Waves and HortPark have barrier-free ramps. Portions of the elevated Forest Walk feature gentle incline grading; other links involve staircase descents into Mount Faber.
openingHours: Open 24 hours daily (Bridge lights illuminate 7:00 PM – 7:00 AM)

name: Fort Canning Park
shortDescription: Historic hilltop park steeped in 14th-century royal heritage and spice gardens.
description: An iconic green hilltop in the centre of the civic district. Once known as Bukit Larangan (Forbidden Hill), it features 9 historical gardens including the Spice Garden, Sang Nila Utama Garden with Javanese architecture, Pancur Larangan bathing spring, and the dramatic spiral staircase tree tunnel at Fort Canning Tree Tunnel.
accessibilityInfo: Covered escalators and elevators connect directly from Fort Canning MRT station (DT20) to the upper lawns. Smooth paved paths link the key gardens.
openingHours: Open 24 hours daily (Gardens illuminated at night)

name: Jurong Lake Gardens
shortDescription: Singapore’s national gardens in the heartlands with freshwater swamp habitats.
description: A 90-hectare biodiversity haven sculpted around Jurong Lake. The development restored naturalized waterways, created the Rasau Walk boardwalk along freshwater swamp vegetation, restored Heron Island for wading birds, and features the poetic Grasslands habitat swaying with lalang and mission grasses.
accessibilityInfo: Fully wheelchair and stroller accessible with wide concrete and wooden promenade pathways throughout Rasau Walk and Lakeside Field.

name: Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park
shortDescription: Landmark biophilic transformation of a concrete storm canal into a living meandering river.
description: One of the world’s most celebrated ecological engineering projects. A former 2.7-km straight concrete stormwater canal was de-concretized and transformed into a 3.2-km natural meandering river with bioengineered soil bio-retaining riverbanks, wildflower floodplains, and thriving wildlife populations.
accessibilityInfo: Entire park is gently contoured with wide asphalt and paved jogging/cycling tracks. Step-free access across all footbridges.
openingHours: Open 24 hours daily (River lighting until 10:00 PM)

name: East Coast Park
shortDescription: 15-kilometre scenic coastal park lined with Casuarina groves and sea breeze recreation.
description: Spanning 185 hectares along Singapore’s southeastern coastline, East Coast Park is the nation’s most beloved coastal recreation haven. Casuarina, ketapang, and coconut palms provide continuous sea-front shade for cycling, birding, and coastal habitat restoration along the Straits of Singapore.
accessibilityInfo: Entire 15-km length features dual wide paved tracks (separate pedestrian walking and cycling corridors) with ramped underpass connections.

name: Labrador Nature Reserve & Coastal Walk
shortDescription: Only rocky sea cliff on mainland Singapore, harbouring rare coastal dipterocarp flora.
description: A unique sanctuary combining historical World War II artillery remains with Singapore’s sole mainland coastal rocky cliff. The reserve houses coastal dipterocarp trees, a boardwalk across mangrove creeks, and open sea vistas facing Sentosa and passing vessels.
accessibilityInfo: Berlayer Creek Boardwalk and Bukit Chermin Boardwalk are fully accessible wooden paths. The elevated hill gun emplacement trail contains stone steps.

name: Pulau Ubin & Chek Jawa Wetlands
shortDescription: Rustic island sanctuary housing six distinct intertidal and coastal ecosystems.
description: An offshore sanctuary preserving Singapore’s 1960s rural heritage (kampong) and natural biodiversity. At its eastern tip lies Chek Jawa, an extraordinary 100-hectare wetland where six distinct ecosystems meet: coastal forest, mangroves, sand bars, seagrass lagoon, rocky shore, and coral rubble.
accessibilityInfo: Bumboat transport requires boarding step. Once on Chek Jawa, the 1.1-km coastal and mangrove boardwalk loop is step-free with anti-slip timber battens.
openingHours: 8:30 AM – 6:00 PM (Chek Jawa Wetlands); Bumboats run 6:00 AM – 7:00 PM

name: Thomson Nature Park
shortDescription: Buffer park conserving the ruins of a former Hainan village amidst dense forest.
description: Opened in 2019, Thomson Nature Park acts as a vital ecological buffer for the Central Catchment Nature Reserve. It provides refuge for the critically endangered Raffles’ Banded Langur monkey. Five heritage trails wind past conserved stone ruins of a 1930s Hainan village engulfed by strangler figs.
accessibilityInfo: Stream and Ferns Trail features well-maintained raised boardwalks with ramp access from the main entrance pavilion. Ruins Trail has stabilized natural ground paths.

name: The Rail Corridor (Green Corridor)
shortDescription: 24-kilometre continuous ecological green spine spanning the length of Singapore.
description: A 24-km linear public green spine reclaimed along the former Keretapi Tanah Melayu (KTM) railway track. Connecting Woodlands in the north to Tanjong Pagar in the south, the corridor links vital habitats, preserves heritage truss bridges, and features dark-sky sensitive lighting to safeguard nocturnal wildlife.
accessibilityInfo: Major restored sections (Central and South) feature porous naturalistic gravel paving with barrier-free ramp access at Bukit Timah Railway Station, King Albert Park, and Holland Road.
openingHours: Open 24 hours daily (Certain sensitive nature stretches are unlit at night to protect wildlife)

name: Coney Island Park (Pulau Serangoon)
shortDescription: Off-grid coastal island with pristine casuarina woodlands, mangrove belts, and secluded beaches.
description: A 133-hectare ecologically sustainable island off Punggol. Operating entirely off-grid without mains electricity or municipal water, it utilizes solar energy and collected rainwater. The island features coastal forests, grasslands, mangroves, and five natural sandy beaches facing the Johor Strait.
accessibilityInfo: Main spine path is a hard-packed gravel track suitable for all-terrain strollers and sturdy wheelchairs. Boardwalk through mangrove trail is step-free.
openingHours: 7:00 AM – 7:00 PM daily (Gates locked outside opening hours)

name: Chestnut Nature Park
shortDescription: Singapore’s largest nature park with separate dedicated mountain biking and hiking trails.
description: Covering 81 hectares across its Northern and Southern parcels, Chestnut Nature Park buffers the Central Catchment. It is Singapore’s first park to feature separate trails for hikers and mountain bikers, reducing user conflict while protecting regenerating native dipterocarp saplings.
accessibilityInfo: Paved amenities pavilion and Chestnut Observation Tower have accessible ramps. Hiking trails are natural earth trails with leaf litter and occasional rock steps.

name: Windsor Nature Park
shortDescription: A rare freshwater swamp forest reserve with elevated boardwalks and rare native ferns.
description: A 75-hectare buffer park that protects freshwater swamp forest habitats. A specially designed marsh habitat and raised boardwalks allow visitors to inspect rare native flora such as the endangered Hanguana rubescens plant and discover over 50 species of dragonflies in the freshwater streams.
accessibilityInfo: The Hanguana Trail is a barrier-free raised wooden boardwalk gently winding through marshland. The Drongo Trail leads to a scenic sub-canopy walkway.

name: Dairy Farm Nature Park
shortDescription: Former cow farm converted into an ecological park with dramatic Singapore Quarry wetlands.
description: A 63-hectare park with rich agricultural and geology history. A former Friesian cow dairy farm established in the 1930s, it now features the Wallace Education Centre with interactive exhibits on Alfred Russel Wallace, and the dramatic Singapore Quarry—a flooded granite quarry against sheer cliff faces hosting wetland birds.
accessibilityInfo: Paved road leading to the Singapore Quarry viewing platform is barrier-free and flat. Wallace Trail has natural earth steps.
